description: The SPR Quick Facts page of the US Department of Energy describes the federally owned Strategic Petroleum Reserve, four sites on the Gulf coast of Texas and Louisiana that hold crude oil in salt dome caverns. A table gives crude oil inventory by site as of 20 August 2026, split into sweet and sour volumes and number of caverns: Bayou Choctaw 32 million barrels in 6 caverns, Big Hill 89.1 in 14, Bryan Mound 142.5 in 19 and West Hackberry 30.5 in 22, for a total of 294.1 million barrels in 61 caverns, against a current authorised capacity of 714 million barrels. It also lists the record inventory of 726.6 million barrels on 27 December 2009, earlier hurricane milestones and emergency releases after Katrina, Gustav and Ike, and the days of import protection, 125 days at the end of 2025 against a 90-day International Energy Agency requirement. Access: free to read on the DOE site, with a link to historical inventory on the EIA website; no download or licence is stated. Coverage is the four SPR sites. Caveats: the page is a summary, not a downloadable data set, and historical series sit on the EIA site. It suits capacity planning and resilience studies of fuel supply, and relates to the EIA petroleum supply and prices record catalogued here.
